description: A two-panel composite figure of dark-field transmission electron micrographs (TEM) comparing the aged microstructure of two Fe-Mn-Al-Si-C cast steels. (a) is the 0.59% Si steel and (b) is the 1.56% Si steel, both aged 63 h at 490-C per the caption. Both panels use the same imaging mode: a dark, uniformly textured austenite matrix speckled with bright nanoscale precipitate particles, which appear as scattered white dots and short bright clusters. Each panel carries its own 10 nm scale bar in the lower-left corner (a white bar on a black rectangle labelled "10 nm"), so precipitate sizes and spacings are directly comparable between panels. In the upper-right corner of each panel there is an inset selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern: a dark square containing a regular array of bright diffraction spots, indicating a crystalline phase on a zone axis; the spot arrays of the two insets appear to be of the same type. The bright precipitate population in (b) is visibly denser, more numerous and more uniformly dispersed than the sparse, patchy bright flecks in (a). The figure therefore demonstrates visually that raising Si from 0.59 to 1.56 wt.% increases both the number density and the apparent size of the carbide precipitates after identical aging, supporting the claim that Si accelerates carbide formation and raises its volume fraction.
measured_quantities: precipitate size (nm, visual against the 10 nm scale bar)

observations.observation: Both panels are dark-field TEM images showing bright nanoscale precipitate particles dispersed in a dark matrix, both with a white 10 nm scale bar on a black rectangle at the lower-left.
Each panel contains a small SAED inset in the upper-right corner displaying a regular array of bright diffraction spots, consistent with a crystalline phase imaged on a zone axis.
The bright precipitate population in panel (b) is visibly denser and more numerous than in panel (a) at the same magnification and scale bar.
Panel (a) is identified in the caption as the 0.59% Si steel aged for 63 h at 490-C.
Panel (b) is identified in the caption as the 1.56% Si steel aged for 63 h at 490-C.
The caption states that the size and number density of 'j-carbide' appear greater with increasing silicon (as printed in the caption text).
The citing text asserts that increasing the amount of silicon accelerated formation of 'j-carbide' precipitates and appears to increase the volume fraction.
The citing text states that in solution-treated specimens XRD and TEM confirmed no spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite regardless of Si content.

The citing text reports a carbon partitioning coefficient for the carbide of 2.1 versus 2.9 in the 0.59% and 1.56% Si steels aged 60 h at 530-C (a different aging condition from the 490-C, 63 h shown in this figure).
The citing text gives a predicted yield-strength increase of 120 MPa/wt.% Si for specimens aged at 530-C for 60 h.
No numeric precipitate size or number-density values are printed on either panel; only the 10 nm scale bar provides a length reference.
The caption labels the imaged phase as 'j-carbide' (as printed), while the citing text refers to the same phase as 'j-carbide' precipitates; the two spelling conventions differ in the source text.

subfigures.description: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the 0.59% Si steel aged 63 h at 490-C. Dark austenite matrix with relatively sparse bright nanoscale precipitates, arranged in patchy clusters. White 10 nm scale bar on a black rectangle at lower-left; a SAED pattern inset with a regular bright spot array occupies the upper-right corner.

Dark-field TEM micrograph of the 1.56% Si steel aged 63 h at 490-C. Same imaging mode and the same 10 nm scale bar, but the bright precipitate particles are markedly more numerous, denser and more evenly distributed across the field than in (a). A SAED inset with a regular bright spot array is again present at upper-right.

unreadable_items: SAED inset diffraction patterns are too small/low-resolution to read individual spot indices or zone axes
no numerical precipitate size or number-density scale or label is printed on either panel
